correctness.rationale: Final result at /workspace/repairs/2/RESULT.md. The original proof's unqualified endpoint-only minimizer was false below the frontier: for example n=2, λ=1, τ=0 gives both weights u>0, so endpoint samples (1,1) produce 2u>0, whereas (0,0) realizes the minimum 0. The corrected proof sets samples to 1 on strictly negative coefficients, 0 on strictly positive coefficients, with zeros free, and distinguishes the two regimes. The original weight and negative-mass formulas do not change. The cross-covariance of the integral with Y is the original kernel mean (2−r^{i−1}−r^{n−i})/λ because the offset is independent of the integrand. The tridiagonal AR(1) inverse verified row by row (including the two endpoints for n=2) gives Qm=u(1,2,…,2,1) and Q1=(1,1−r,…,1−r,1)/(1+r). Thus w=Qm−(τ·2(n−1)u/D)Q1 and the endpoint numerator reduces to u(1−(n−2)τ), while the interior numerator is 2u(1+τ). All denominators and interior numerators are positive; this includes no offset and zero endpoints at equality, and n=2 has no finite boundary. Given h=1/(n−1), u/h→1/2 and D→1+τ(1+λ/2); separating the two endpoints from the interior Riemann sum gives the signed weak limit against every continuous function. For independent noise, (I+ηQ)w=Qm. At a nonpositive minimum coordinate, the positive row sum and nonpositive off-diagonals would give a nonpositive left-side component, contradicting Qm>0. Independent numerical replay of 136 bounded direct covariance systems matched the weights within 1.492×10⁻¹¹; 16 diagonal-nugget solves were positive; weak-limit diagnostics up to n=2000 corroborated convergence. Evidence and replay details: /workspace/branches/5012c8b8-039e-434d-beb2-406d2f93f559/independent-check.md. The submitted code was read, not run. Numerical tests are diagnostics, not uniform proofs or authority for mixed noise models.

evidence: The strongest close corpus result proves subprobability for arbitrary ordered sites, positive target measures and all diagonal nuggets. It covers nonnegativity here for independent noise and strict positivity when η>0; η=0 follows directly from Qm.

evidence: The rank-one update is standard and yields a Q1 correction; the new sign cancellation uses the different endpoint/interior components of Q1 and Qm as well as unchanged integral cross-covariance. In the dense limit the endpoint correction stays order one while the weight at an interior node is order h.

evidence: The model is equivalent to simple Gaussian block prediction of the integral of a latent OU field given noisy levels, covariance of data K+τ11ᵀ and cross-covariance m. It is also equivalent to conditioning on the observed level plus a random intercept and subtracting the inferred intercept from the observed-level integral.

Karvonen et al. use the kernel mean cross-covariance of the observed noiseless process, while ordinary unknown-mean prediction generally imposes unbiasedness rather than a finite random-offset variance.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: If the constant term belongs to the integrated process, the cross-covariance becomes m+τ1; the difference in the weights is +τQ1/D. The fitted-integrand problem with this added term is not an equivalent proof of the offset frontier. A known GLS constant-level estimator can supply Q1, one ingredient, but not the stated finite rank-one-offset sign claim on its own.

originality.rationale: The verified surviving contribution is the common-measurement-offset threshold and signed dense limit; Gaussian conditioning, AR(1) precision, and Sherman–Morrison are prior methods. The independent-noise statement is explicitly comparative in the repaired result, with the stronger diagonal-nugget finding cited. The corrected sharpness witness is not claimed as novel in isolation.
residual_risks: Unindexed correlated-error kriging, Gaussian random-intercept prediction, or classical continuous-time regression may contain equivalent adjoint formulas or the same finite sign theorem. The comparison does not certify historical priority.
The related result about diagonal nuggets should not be counted as originality for this common-offset record.

value.rationale: The finite threshold answers when nonnegative readings can yield a negative posterior integral estimate under a simple sensor-calibration model, with a sharp worst-case magnitude and exact correlation-length cancellation. The sign effect does not disappear with arbitrarily many observations at fixed positive shared variance; the limit identifies its boundary atoms. This is a structural stability result, not a claim that positive weights guarantee lower numerical or statistical error. The minimizer repair makes the operational interpretation correct in all regimes without weakening those contributions.
